newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar pauses for breath, Eurobourses down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar pauses for breath, Eurobourses down.

text.p: The dollar consolidated in morning European trade on Wednesday after a two-day rally sparked by central bank comments while on the stock exchanges, leading shares were trading marginally lower.

Currency dealers said the dollar had hit strong resistance at 1.5120 marks and a psychological barrier at 110 yen. At 0930 it was trading at 1.5125 marks and 110.20 yen. Last Friday the U.S. currency had closed in London at 1.4913 marks and 109.32 yen.

Analysts said the underlying tone of the dollar remained positive amid speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates later this month when its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets.

Comments by Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen on Tuesday added impetus to the dollar rally. Yellen suggested the U.S. economy looked vulnerable to inflation -- reinforcing the markets' feeling that there is an interest rate rise to come.

For a dollar recovery beyond the 1.52-mark region that prevailed before July, the Fed would have to raise rates by 50 basis points, said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
He believed a widely expected 25 basis point rise would be fairly neutral for the dollar.

On the bourses, London shares opened mixed after the release of a string of company results at the start of trade and with Wall Street, which closed 6.66 down at 5727.18, failing to provide a firm lead overnight.
By 0930 GMT the blue chip FTSE 100 index had edged 3.8 points lower to 3912.3 as the market digested interim figures from Prudential, Mirror Group, and Kingfisher among others.

On Tuesday the FTSE hit, but failed to maintain, a new intraday high of 3933.6. Traders said it could well challenge record territory again this week, with many still talking of 4,000 as a feasible short-term target.
The publication on Wednesday of fresh British employment and earnings data left the market virtually unmoved.

The unemployment rate fell to 7.5 percent in August, from 7.6 in July, after the number of jobless fell 15,600 to 2.11 million. The figures were in line with market expectations and the Treasury said they underlined strengthening economic activity.

In Frankfurt German shares opened bourse trade marginally lower, dragged down by the weaker overnight close of the Dow Jones Average but supported by a firm dollar against the mark -- which makes German exports more attractive.
French shares also started weaker on consolidation, then came off their lows. "The market has been climbing for five days. It needs to breathe a bit," one trader said.
A big loser was carmaker Renault, down 7.82 percent after it reported late Tuesday a big slide in first-half profits.

On the precious metals market, palladium slid to its lowest fix in more than 33 months as speculators liquidated positions, dealers said. Palladium fixed at $123 an ounce, the lowest since December 29, 1993, and $1 lower than Tuesday afternoon.

A dealers said one reason has been steady selling from Russia, the world's largest producer, during the slack summer season when European industry was closed and demand was low. A major use of the rare metal is in automotive exhaust catalysts.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5125 marks and 110.15 yen compared with Tuesday's London close of 1.5087 marks and 109.80 yen.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 3.8 points at 3,912.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 5.89 at 2,036.23.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 4.59 at 2,566.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $383.15 against Tuesday's European close of 383.45. The market was very quiet and consolidating in $382-$385 range. But vulnerable to downside, with $380 as the next key level.
